621	    """
622	    Parse the lang_string, which is the body of an HTTP Accept-Language
623	    header, and return a tuple of (lang, q-value), ordered by 'q' values.

625	    Return an empty tuple if there are any format errors in lang_string.

629	    if pieces[-1]:

631	    for i in range(0, len(pieces) - 1, 3):
632	        first, lang, priority = pieces[i : i + 3]
633	        if first:
634	            return ()
635	        if priority:
636	            priority = float(priority)
637	        else:
638	            priority = 1.0

641	    return tuple(result)

644	def parse_accept_lang_header(lang_string):
645	    """
646	    Parse the value of the Accept-Language header up to a maximum length.
647	
648	    The value of the header is truncated to a maximum length to avoid potential
649	    denial of service and memory exhaustion attacks. Excessive memory could be
650	    used if the raw value is very large as it would be cached due to the use of
651	    functools.lru_cache() to avoid repetitive parsing of common header values.
652	    """
653	    # If the header value doesn't exceed the maximum allowed length, parse it.
654	    if len(lang_string) <= LANGUAGE_CODE_MAX_LENGTH:
655	        return _parse_accept_lang_header(lang_string)
656	
657	    # If there is at least one comma in the value, parse up to the last comma
658	    # before the max length, skipping any truncated parts at the end of the
659	    # header value.
660	    if (index := lang_string.rfind(",", 0, LANGUAGE_CODE_MAX_LENGTH)) > 0:
661	        return _parse_accept_lang_header(lang_string[:index])
662	
663	    # Don't attempt to parse if there is only one language-range value which is

665	    return ()

641	    This class implements shuffling with a special consistency property.
642	    Consistency means that, for a given seed and key function, if two sets of
643	    items are shuffled, the resulting order will agree on the intersection of
644	    the two sets. For example, if items are removed from an original set, the
645	    shuffled order for the new set will be the shuffled order of the original
646	    set restricted to the smaller set.

12	    def optimize(self, operations, app_label):
13	        """

15	        get out a new list of Operation instances.
16	
17	        Unfortunately, due to the scope of the optimization (two combinable
18	        operations might be separated by several hundred others), this can't be
19	        done as a peephole optimization with checks/output implemented on
20	        the Operations themselves; instead, the optimizer looks at each
21	        individual operation and scans forwards in the list to see if there
22	        are any matches, stopping at boundaries - operations which can't
23	        be optimized over (RunSQL, operations on the same field/model, etc.)
24	
25	        The inner loop is run until the starting list is the same as the result
26	        list, and then the result is returned. This means that operation
27	        optimization must be stable and always return an equal or shorter list.
28	        """
29	        # Internal tracking variable for test assertions about # of loops
30	        if app_label is None:
31	            raise TypeError("app_label must be a str.")
32	        self._iterations = 0
33	        while True:
34	            result = self.optimize_inner(operations, app_label)
35	            self._iterations += 1
36	            if result == operations:
37	                return result
38	            operations = result

41	        """Inner optimization loop."""
42	        new_operations = []
43	        for i, operation in enumerate(operations):
44	            right = True  # Should we reduce on the right or on the left.
45	            # Compare it to each operation after it
46	            for j, other in enumerate(operations[i + 1 :]):
47	                result = operation.reduce(other, app_label)
48	                if isinstance(result, list):
49	                    in_between = operations[i + 1 : i + j + 1]
50	                    if right:
51	                        new_operations.extend(in_between)
52	                        new_operations.extend(result)
53	                    elif all(op.reduce(other, app_label) is True for op in in_between):
54	                        # Perform a left reduction if all of the in-between
55	                        # operations can optimize through other.
56	                        new_operations.extend(result)
57	                        new_operations.extend(in_between)
58	                    else:
59	                        # Otherwise keep trying.
60	                        new_operations.append(operation)
61	                        break
62	                    new_operations.extend(operations[i + j + 2 :])
63	                    return new_operations

28	    def get_template(self, template_name, skip=None):
29	        """
30	        Perform the caching that gives this loader its name. Often many of the
31	        templates attempted will be missing, so memory use is of concern here.
32	        To keep it in check, caching behavior is a little complicated when a
33	        template is not found. See ticket #26306 for more details.
34	
35	        With template debugging disabled, cache the TemplateDoesNotExist class
36	        for every missing template and raise a new instance of it after
37	        fetching it from the cache.
38	
39	        With template debugging enabled, a unique TemplateDoesNotExist object
40	        is cached for each missing template to preserve debug data. When
41	        raising an exception, Python sets __traceback__, __context__, and
42	        __cause__ attributes on it. Those attributes can contain references to
43	        all sorts of objects up the call chain and caching them creates a
44	        memory leak. Thus, unraised copies of the exceptions are cached and
45	        copies of those copies are raised after they're fetched from the cache.
46	        """

48	        cached = self.get_template_cache.get(key)
49	        if cached:
50	            if isinstance(cached, type) and issubclass(cached, TemplateDoesNotExist):
51	                raise cached(template_name)
52	            elif isinstance(cached, TemplateDoesNotExist):
53	                raise copy_exception(cached)
54	            return cached
55

57	            template = super().get_template(template_name, skip)
58	        except TemplateDoesNotExist as e:
59	            self.get_template_cache[key] = (
60	                copy_exception(e) if self.engine.debug else TemplateDoesNotExist
61	            )
62	            raise
63	        else:
64	            self.get_template_cache[key] = template
65	
66	        return template

69	        for loader in self.loaders:
70	            yield from loader.get_template_sources(template_name)

73	        """

76	        If skip is provided, only origins that match template_name are included
77	        in the cache key. This ensures each template is only parsed and cached
78	        once if contained in different extend chains like:
79	
80	            x -> a -> a
81	            y -> a -> a
82	            z -> a -> a
83	        """
84	        skip_prefix = ""
85	
86	        if skip:

89	            ]
